guide.title: A race-condition case about fixing the violated invariant, not the request's latest disguise.
guide.problem: Two requests arrived milliseconds apart, both read the booking session as available, and both created airline records. The guard was check-then-act across a 25 ms window; its optimistic-lock timestamp had only one-second resolution.
guide.core_idea: Make the state transition a conditional database write using a monotonic VERSION column. Exactly one request updates the expected version; affected-row count identifies the winner without leaving a gap between check and act.
guide.outcome: A User-Agent block suppressed one trigger and stopped alerts for two and a half years, but the race returned as HEAD. The final fix combined database-enforced optimistic locking, explicit HEAD rejection and deterministic concurrency tests.
takeaways: Check-then-act is not mutual exclusion: two requests can read the same state before either write becomes visible, even when the code looks correct sequentially.
A timestamp whose resolution is coarser than request arrival is not a reliable version token; higher precision lowers probability but does not create a guarantee.
Blocking a User-Agent or HTTP method removes a known trigger, not the race. Correctness belongs at the shared database transition every contender must cross.
Affected-row count turns optimistic locking into an explicit decision: one conditional update succeeds, all losing contenders observe zero updated rows.
The row version protects one session, not the whole booking intent. Cross-session retries still need an idempotency key backed by a unique constraint.
review_lenses: Invariant: which business effect must happen exactly once, and which shared row or unique key can adjudicate it atomically?
Concurrency: where is the read/write gap, and can requests reach it through different processes, methods, retries or devices?
Evidence: do quiet alerts prove the invariant, or only that one observed trigger has stopped producing the old signature?
Verification: can a barrier or injected delay reproduce the race deterministically and assert exactly one committed side effect?
